title: Candidate Immersion: 72hr Technical Sandbox Onboarding
body:
Purpose and scope:
This document defines a short-form (72 hour) candidate immersion path we use for late-stage technical interviews and contract-to-perm conversion pilots. The goal is to give candidates a realistic sandbox where they demonstrate work habits, communication, and ship a small, observable piece of work rather than just whiteboard answers. This is intended for mid+ IC roles (SWE2/3, Infra, ML-FE) and short contract engagements used as extended auditions.

When to use:
- Offer contingent on successful 72hr sandbox (rare; only for senior IC and high-impact roles).
- Contract-to-perm evaluation: run during week 1 of contract as a shared artifact for conversion decisions.
- Alternative to long take-home assignments when speed and context matter.

High-level timeline (72 hours):
- Hour 0: kickoff email + access provisioned (repo, infra sandbox, Slack channel, brief).
- Hour 1–8: orientation + small discovery task (read docs, run local dev, smoke tests).
- Day 1 (hours 9–24): implement scoped feature or bugfix (small vertical). Daily stand check-in at hour 18.
- Day 2 (hours 25–48): continue feature, add tests, address review comments, produce short README describing decisions.
- Day 3 (hours 49–72): polish, integration test, deploy to ephemeral environment (if applicable), final 30–45 minute demo to interviewing panel + debrief.

Kickoff checklist (People Ops / Hiring Manager):
- Create ephemeral repo fork from sandbox template and add candidate as a collaborator with 72 hour expiration.
- Provision cloud sandbox credentials (read-only by default; scoped service account) and CI runner if needed.
- Create a dedicated Slack thread + invite hiring panel and candidate.
- Populate candidate brief with context, acceptance criteria, and suggested reading links.
- Add calendar invites: 30-minute kickoff (optional), 30-minute demo + 30-minute debrief.
- Notify security to apply temporary project-level audit logging.

Candidate brief (example, included in repo README):
- Background: short description of product area, data constraints, and why this change matters.
- Task: small, scoped ask (~2–6 hours of focused code) with clear acceptance criteria (unit tests passing, e2e smoke, API contract).
- Deliverable: branch with tests + short PR, README describing tradeoffs, 10–12 minute demo in panel meeting.
- Constraints: no internet-dependent secrets; use provided mock dataset; prefer small API-first change.

Interview rubric (simplified, panel uses same sheet to score) — all items scored 1–5, notes required for 1–2 or 4–5:
- Problem framing and tradeoff articulation (weight 20%)
- Code correctness and test coverage (weight 25%)
- Design for operability (observability, deployability, rollback plan) (weight 15%)
- Communication and collaboration (opens PR early, addresses feedback, clear commit messages) (weight 15%)
- Velocity and prioritization (delivers a working slice within timebox) (weight 10%)
- Cultural fit signals (alignment with team values; curiosity) (weight 10%)

Scoring rules:
- Each panelist assigns 1–5 for each category and writes a 1–2 sentence rationale.
- Weighted score = sum(category_score * category_weight). Convert weights to decimals (e.g., 0.2).
- Thresholds (recommendation guidance only):
  - >=4.2: strong yes (recommend hire/convert)
  - 3.5–4.19: consider, but review open risks and schedule follow-up interview
  - <3.5: recommend no

Debrief template (to paste into the hiring doc):
- Candidate: [name]
- Role: [title]
- Date: [YYYY-MM-DD]
- Panel: [names]
- Deliverable summary (2–3 sentences):
- What went well (bullets):
- Areas of risk / questions left open (bullets):
- Score summary (weighted total + per-category averages):
- Recommendation: [hire/conditional/decline] and rationale
- Proposed next steps (if conditional): [e.g., 1-week extended contract, follow-up system design, mentorship pairing]

Operational guardrails and security notes:
- Sandbox credentials must be scoped read-only for data; service accounts used for CI must expire automatically.
- No production DB credentials in any candidate repo. If a limited repro of production data is needed, use masked sample dataset provided by infra team.
- Retain audit logs for 30 days and mark the ephemeral repo with a retention tag.

Handoff checklist for contract-to-perm conversion (if candidate becomes perm):
- Consolidate PRs and merge into main internal onboarding branch.
- Transfer ownership of ephemeral repo into team org with access audit.
- Capture a 1-page summary of candidate tradeoffs and implemented design for their onboarding doc.
- Schedule a 1:1 with hiring manager within first 3 business days for goal alignment.

Example scoring snippet (panel copy-paste):
- Framing: 4
- Correctness: 4
- Operability: 3
- Communication: 5
- Velocity: 4
- Culture: 4
Weighted total = 4*0.2 + 4*0.25 + 3*0.15 + 5*0.15 + 4*0.10 + 4*0.10 = 0.8 + 1.0 + 0.45 + 0.75 + 0.4 + 0.4 = 3.8 (recommend: hire with minor onboarding focus)

Administrative templates (short):
- Kickoff email subject: "Redwood sandbox kickoff — [candidate name] — 72h"
- Kickoff email body (short): "Hi [candidate], welcome — repo link: [URL], slack: [URL], brief: [README link]. Please ping in the thread if you hit infra issues. We’ll demo on [date/time]. Best, [hiring manager]"
- Demo invite description: "10–15 minute walkthrough + 15–20 min Q&A and debrief. Panel: [names]."

Notes to people ops / hiring managers (things we learned):
- Keep acceptance criteria minimal and measurable; avoid open-ended product asks that require 2+ days of discovery.
- Encourage early PRs and small commits so reviewers can provide incremental feedback — that’s a signal we want to surface.
- For ML and infra roles, prefer reproducible notebooks or short infra templates rather than large model training jobs.

Open questions / follow-ups (action items):
- (Priya) define template for ephemeral credential provisioning automation (due 2026-03-15).
- (Ellen) propose standard masked sample datasets for common product domains (due 2026-03-22).
- (People Ops) review legal language for contingent offers that reference this evaluation step.

Appendix: quick links
- Ephemeral repo template: github.com/redwood-inference/onboarding-sandbox-template
- Credential rotation playbook: confluence.redwood/infra/ephemeral-credentials
- Audit logging SOP: confluence.redwood/security/audit-sop

End of doc.
